analysis:
This batch contains only documentation: a new changelog.d entry (changelog.d/fused-causal-prefill-attention.md, lines 1-5) and one added table row in docs/architecture/inference.md at head line 1090. No executable code, keys, protocol messages, attestation paths, cache storage, or authorization logic is changed here. The docs describe an Attention change in the MLX Swift library (AttentionV1.swift `usesFusedCausalPrefill`, PagedLayerCache.swift `prefillAttend`). That change is not in the supplied batch, so it was not reviewed.

Security-relevant observations for later passes:
- The documented fused `.causal` prefill path applies to full-attention chunks only. Sliding-window, softcapped, vision-span, live packed paged KV and Gemma 4 layers are said to be unchanged. Whether the fused path can break per-request isolation (mask correctness, paged KV block boundaries, prefix-cache adoption offsets) cannot be verified without the Swift source. Relevant threat IDs: T-041, T-028, TB-007.
- The changelog says `DARKBLOOM_TTFT_FUSED_CAUSAL_PREFILL=0` is not delivered to the provider LaunchAgent. That is an operational kill-switch limitation, not a security control change.
- The changelog says Qwen output on M5 can differ within bf16 rounding. Nemotron 3.5 Lightning and the other qualifying models were not measured. That is a correctness/qualification caveat, not a confidentiality issue.
- The changelog describes TTFT reductions. That may marginally change the cache hit/miss timing delta, but SEC-035 already accepts the TTFT oracle in kind. No new exposure is evident from documentation alone.

No findings. The actual code diff, if present in other batches, needs review for mask or causal-offset correctness and memory-bound changes. Neither can be confirmed from these docs.
